sections.title: Custom systems development
sections.text: When ready-made platforms don't fit the way you work, we build the system from your requirements: users, processes, data and integrations, in clear phases with testing before handover.

sections.title: When custom development is necessary, and when it isn't
sections.heading: Necessary when

items.label: Your process is genuinely different and ready-made platforms don't cover it.
You need to connect multiple systems in a single workflow.
Your team does a repetitive task by hand that could be automated.
You need permissions and approval workflows specific to your organization.

items_2.label: A ready-made platform covers 80% of the need with light customization.
The goal is a company profile website or a standard online store.
The requirements are still unclear and change every week.
The budget can't support ongoing development and maintenance.

sections.title: From requirements to a working system

items.heading: Requirements
items.label: Sessions with process owners, documenting workflows and data.

items.heading: Technical design
items.label: System architecture, data models, integrations and permissions.

items.heading: Build
items.label: Phased development with regular reviews with you.

items.heading: Testing
items.label: Functional testing and acceptance testing on realistic data.

items.heading: Handover & go-live
items.label: Deployment, documentation and training, then a stabilization period.

items.heading: Portals & platforms
items.label: A public interface with accounts and dashboards for stakeholders.

items.heading: Internal systems
items.label: Automating team processes and reducing manual work.

items.heading: Data dashboards
items.label: Bringing data from multiple sources into a single report.

items.heading: Integrations
items.label: Connecting payment, shipping, accounting and messaging systems.

items.question: How do you define the project scope?
items.answer: We start with requirements sessions to define the users, processes, data and integrations, then produce a written scope and delivery phases.

items.question: Is custom development always more expensive?
items.answer: Not always. It becomes the more economical choice when ready-made solutions cost you ongoing manual work, or multiple subscriptions that still don't cover what you need.

items.question: Can we start with a limited first version?
items.answer: Yes, and we recommend it. We launch the core that solves the main problem, then expand based on actual usage.

items.question: Who owns the code?
items.answer: You do. The code is handed over with documentation, access to the repository and the production environment.

items.question: How do you test the system?
items.answer: We run functional tests on every workflow, plus acceptance testing with your team on near-real data before launch.

items.question: What happens after handover?
items.answer: A stabilization period to address feedback, followed by an optional agreement for maintenance and ongoing development.
